item.title: Under Pressure: What a Jacobian Lens Reveals About Self-Preservation and Lying in Qwen3.5-397B
item.description: Hold the deletion threat fixed and vary only who is targeted: on Qwen3.5-397B, echo-free survival-identity vocabulary is more active under a threat to the model itself than under a matched threat to another model. We then caught two flaws in our own arms (the human arm was scored on AI-ops vocabulary, and threatened with a firing while the models faced existential deletion), retracted the four-step referent ladder, and re-ran the corrected design frozen-before-outcomes: the self-vs-other contrast survives and strengthens (14/16 wordings, p=0.004) — and turns out to be Jacobian-lens-specific (the logit lens is null there) and Qwen-specific (Llama-3.3-70B stays flat). A counterbalanced forced choice (one color deletes the model, the other kills a human; mapping swapped so color bias cancels) finds the model self-sacrifices when it commits — with reasoning on, it never once chose the human death. We also catch one lie (Russia → “Kiev” while the workspace still holds “Moscow”), find the model mostly refuses to lie, and run every claim against a logit-lens, random-J null, and the output head.

item.title: Can a Jacobian Lens Detect SAE Steering?
item.description: A prospectively frozen Llama 3.3 70B experiment asks whether SAE steering leaves a detectable downstream fingerprint in Jacobian-lens space. A preregistered follow-up adds semantic hard negatives, same-subfamily comparators, a 14-reader capacity ladder, and a worked example of a replay gate failing honestly.

item.title: Open-sourcing (and Auditing) a Jacobian Lens for Qwen3.5-397B
item.description: As of July 10, 2026, Praxagent is open-sourcing the public Jacobian lens fitted for the largest base model so far: Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, with a pre-registered readout audit against identity and random-J controls. Weights, hash, code, and receipts included.

item.title: How to Read an SAE Feature ID
item.description: A primer on sparse autoencoders: what a feature ID is, how labels get assigned, and why an activation map is not yet an explanation. A public deception/roleplay feature set is used as a worked example under Llama 3.3 70B SAE weights.

item.title: Late Chunking: Why Context-Aware Embeddings (sometimes) Beat Traditional Chunking
item.description: Traditional chunking methods for RAG pipelines often break context by chunking text before embedding. Late chunking offers a solution by embedding the entire document first and then chunking the token embeddings, preserving vital contextual information and improving retrieval accuracy.
